pinyin: tù zi wěi ba —— cháng bù liǎo
literal: rabbit · tail — long · cannot
natural: a rabbit's tail

meaning.en: A rabbit's tail is short; something that won't last long.
meaning.zh: 兔子的尾巴很短；比喻事物维持不了多久。

examples.zh: 他那点风光，兔子尾巴，长不了。
examples.en: His moment of glory won't last.

examples.zh: 靠投机赚来的钱是兔子尾巴，长不了。
examples.en: Money made by speculation won't last.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. 长 here means 'long' (cháng) and 'lasting'.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。“长”指“长久”。

pinyin: tuō kù zi fàng pì —— duō cǐ yī jǔ
literal: take off · trousers · let · fart — more · this · one · act
natural: taking off one's trousers to fart

meaning.en: Taking one's trousers off to break wind; an unnecessary, pointless extra step.
meaning.zh: 脱了裤子才放屁，多费一道手续；比喻做了多余的事。

examples.zh: 文件已经发了，你再打印一遍，不是脱裤子放屁吗？
examples.en: The file was already sent; printing it again is pointless.

examples.zh: 这一步纯属脱裤子放屁，删掉吧。
examples.en: This step is utterly unnecessary; delete it.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Vulgar; use among friends only.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。较粗俗，仅限熟人之间使用。

pinyin: duì niú tán qín —— bái fèi jìn
literal: to · ox · play · zither — in vain · waste · effort
natural: playing the zither to an ox

meaning.en: Playing music to an ox; speaking to someone who cannot understand, or wasting effort on the wrong audience.
meaning.zh: 对着牛弹琴，牛听不懂；比喻对不懂道理的人讲道理，白费力气。

examples.zh: 跟他讲艺术，简直是对牛弹琴。
examples.en: Talking to him about art is like casting pearls before swine.

examples.zh: 我说了三遍他都不听，对牛弹琴啊。
examples.en: I told him three times and he wouldn't listen; it's a waste of breath.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. It is also a standalone chengyu, 对牛弹琴.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。也是独立成语“对牛弹琴”。

text: 黄连树下弹琴——苦中作乐
pinyin: huáng lián shù xià tán qín —— kǔ zhōng zuò lè
variants: 黄连树下弹琵琶——苦中作乐
literal: coptis · tree · under · play zither — bitterness · amid · make · joy
natural: playing the zither under a bitter coptis tree

meaning.en: Playing music beneath a bitter-tasting tree; finding a bit of fun in the midst of hardship.
meaning.zh: 黄连味苦，树下弹琴；比喻在困苦中寻找乐趣。

equivalents: make the best of a bad job

examples.zh: 加班到半夜还讲笑话，真是黄连树下弹琴。
examples.en: Telling jokes while working late into the night is making the best of a bad job.

examples.zh: 日子虽然难，他总能黄连树下弹琴。
examples.en: Life is hard, but he always finds something to smile about.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. 黄连 (coptis) is an intensely bitter herb used in medicine.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。黄连是一种极苦的药材。

pinyin: sǐ yā zi —— zuǐ yìng
literal: dead · duck — mouth · hard
natural: a dead duck: only its beak is stiff

meaning.en: A dead duck's beak stays hard; someone who won't admit defeat or error even when beaten.
meaning.zh: 鸭子死了嘴巴还是硬的；比喻明明理亏或失败了，还不肯认输。

examples.zh: 明明错了还不认，真是死鸭子嘴硬。
examples.en: He's clearly wrong but won't admit it; stubborn to the last.

examples.zh: 你别死鸭子，承认吧。
examples.en: Stop being so stubborn and admit it.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Often written 煮熟的鸭子，嘴硬 as well; the second half is sometimes used alone: 嘴硬.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。后半句常单用：“嘴硬”。

text: 茶壶里煮饺子——有口倒不出
pinyin: chá hú lǐ zhǔ jiǎo zi —— yǒu kǒu dào bù chū
literal: teapot · inside · boil · dumplings — have · mouth · pour · not · out
natural: boiling dumplings in a teapot

meaning.en: Dumplings boiled in a teapot can't be poured out; having something to say but not being able to express it.
meaning.zh: 饺子在茶壶里煮熟，倒不出来；比喻心里有话说不出，或有本事施展不开。

examples.zh: 我满肚子委屈，真是茶壶里煮饺子。
examples.en: I'm full of grievances but can't put them into words.

examples.zh: 他的想法很多，可茶壶里煮饺子，表达不出来。
examples.en: He has plenty of ideas but can't express them.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Also means being unable to show one's ability for lack of opportunity.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。也可指有本事却无处施展。

pinyin: zhú tǒng dào dòu zi —— yī gān èr jìng
literal: bamboo · tube · pour · beans — one · dry · two · clean
natural: pouring beans from a bamboo tube

meaning.en: Tipping beans out of a bamboo tube leaves nothing behind; telling everything frankly and completely.
meaning.zh: 竹筒里的豆子倒得干干净净；比喻把话全部说出来，毫无保留。

examples.zh: 警察一问，他就竹筒倒豆子，全说了。
examples.en: As soon as the police asked, he spilled the beans.

examples.zh: 心里话我今天竹筒倒豆子，说个痛快。
examples.en: Today I'll say everything on my mind.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Used for talking frankly, and also for finishing something cleanly.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。既可指畅所欲言，也可指做事干净利落。

pinyin: hóu zi lāo yuè —— bái máng huó
literal: monkey · fish out · moon — in vain · busy · work
natural: monkeys trying to fish the moon from the water

meaning.en: Monkeys try to scoop the moon's reflection from a well; labour that comes to nothing.
meaning.zh: 猴子想捞井里的月亮影子；比喻白白忙碌一场，什么也得不到。

examples.zh: 他们折腾了一年，结果猴子捞月，白忙活。
examples.en: They toiled for a year and got nothing out of it.

examples.zh: 这个项目被砍了，咱们是猴子捞月。
examples.en: The project was cancelled; our effort was wasted.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From a Buddhist fable in which monkeys drown trying to rescue the moon.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。来自猴子捞月亮的寓言故事。

pinyin: yán wáng yé dǎ jià —— xiǎo guǐ zāo yāng
literal: King Yama · fight — little · ghosts · suffer · disaster
natural: the King of Hell brawls and the imps suffer

meaning.en: When the King of Hell fights, his minions suffer; ordinary people are hurt when the powerful quarrel.
meaning.zh: 阎王打架，小鬼倒霉；比喻大人物争斗，下面的人受害。

equivalents: when elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers
small fry suffer when the big fish fight

examples.zh: 两个部门主管吵架，我们小职员阎王爷打架，小鬼遭殃。
examples.en: When two department heads quarrel, we staff suffer.

examples.zh: 大公司打价格战，阎王爷打架，供应商遭殃。
examples.en: In a price war between giants, suppliers get hurt.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。

pinyin: liú bèi jiè jīng zhōu —— yǒu jiè wú huán
literal: Liu Bei · borrow · Jingzhou — have · borrow · no · return
natural: Liu Bei borrows Jingzhou

meaning.en: Liu Bei borrowed Jingzhou from Wu and never returned it; borrowing something and never giving it back.
meaning.zh: 刘备向东吴借荆州，却一直不还；比喻借了东西不还。

equivalents: a loan that is never repaid

examples.zh: 他借我的书就像刘备借荆州，有借无还。
examples.en: Books I lend him never come back.

examples.zh: 你可别刘备借荆州，借了就不还。
examples.en: Don't borrow it and never return it.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From the Three Kingdoms story of Wu's loan of Jingzhou to Shu.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自三国时东吴借荆州给蜀汉的故事。

pinyin: zhāng fēi chuān zhēn —— dà yǎn dèng xiǎo yǎn
literal: Zhang Fei · thread · needle — big · eyes · glare · small · eyes
natural: Zhang Fei threading a needle: big eye glares at small eye

meaning.en: Big-eyed Zhang Fei staring at a needle's tiny eye; two parties staring at each other, helpless or at a loss.
meaning.zh: 张飞的大眼睛盯着针眼；比喻双方面面相觑，没有办法。

examples.zh: 项目出了问题，大家张飞穿针，大眼瞪小眼。
examples.en: The project hit a snag and everyone just stared at each other.

examples.zh: 会议上没人发言，大家只能张飞穿针，大眼瞪小眼。
examples.en: Nobody spoke at the meeting; people just stared at each other.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Zhang Fei is famed for his big eyes and bluff character; a different punchline, 粗中有细, is also heard.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。张飞以大眼睛和粗犷性格著称；也有另一种后半句“粗中有细”。

text: 张飞卖豆腐——人硬货不硬
pinyin: zhāng fēi mài dòu fu —— rén yìng huò bù yìng
variants: 张飞卖豆腐——人强货不硬
literal: Zhang Fei · sell · tofu — man · hard · goods · not · hard
natural: Zhang Fei sells tofu: the seller is tough but the tofu is soft

meaning.en: The seller is burly but the tofu soft; a tough-looking person whose goods or abilities are weak.
meaning.zh: 卖豆腐的人很壮，豆腐却软；比喻人看着厉害，本事或货色不行。

equivalents: a big man with little to offer

examples.zh: 他看上去很厉害，其实是张飞卖豆腐。
examples.en: He looks formidable, but he's got little to back it up.

examples.zh: 张飞卖豆腐，人硬货不硬，别被他唬住。
examples.en: Don't let his bluster scare you; he's got little to offer.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。

text: 猪八戒背媳妇——吃力不讨好
pinyin: zhū bā jiè bēi xí fù —— chī lì bù tǎo hǎo
variants: 猪八戒背媳妇——费力不讨好
literal: Zhu Bajie · carry on back · wife — strenuous · not · win · favour
natural: Pigsy carries his wife on his back

meaning.en: Pigsy carrying his bride; putting in great effort and still getting no thanks.
meaning.zh: 猪八戒背媳妇，累了还不讨好；比喻费力却得不到好评。

equivalents: work hard and get no thanks

examples.zh: 帮他们调解，我真是猪八戒背媳妇。
examples.en: Mediating for them was a thankless task.

examples.zh: 老板还嫌我做得慢，这是猪八戒背媳妇。
examples.en: The boss still complains I'm slow; I get no thanks.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From the episode of 《西游记》 in which Pigsy carries the bride.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。典出《西游记》中猪八戒背新娘的情节。

text: 猪八戒吃人参果——全不知滋味
pinyin: zhū bā jiè chī rén shēn guǒ —— quán bù zhī zī wèi
variants: 猪八戒吃人参果——囫囵吞枣
literal: Zhu Bajie · eat · ginseng fruit — completely · not · know · taste
natural: Pigsy gulps down the ginseng fruit

meaning.en: Pigsy swallowed the rare fruit whole without tasting it; failing to appreciate something good.
meaning.zh: 猪八戒吞下人参果，没尝出味道；比喻不会品味，辜负好东西。

equivalents: fail to appreciate the good stuff

examples.zh: 这么好的茶你一口喝光，真是猪八戒吃人参果。
examples.en: You downed such fine tea in one gulp without tasting it.

examples.zh: 看书太快就是猪八戒吃人参果，收获不大。
examples.en: Reading too fast gets you little out of a book.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Based on 《西游记》, where Pigsy gobbles the ginseng fruit in one bite.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《西游记》，猪八戒一口吞下人参果。

text: 孙悟空翻跟头——一个筋斗十万八千里
pinyin: sūn wù kōng fān gēn tou —— yī gè jīn dǒu shí wàn bā qiān lǐ
variants: 孙悟空翻跟头——一步十万八千里
literal: Sun Wukong · turn · somersault — one · somersault · 108,000 · li
natural: Monkey King's somersault: 108,000 li in one

meaning.en: The Monkey King covers 108,000 li in a single somersault; extremely fast, or a very long way.
meaning.zh: 孙悟空一个筋斗能翻十万八千里；比喻速度极快，或相隔很远。

examples.zh: 他办事效率高，孙悟空翻跟头，转眼就搞定。
examples.en: He's very efficient; in the blink of an eye it's done.

examples.zh: 我们的想法差得远，真是孙悟空翻跟头。
examples.en: Our ideas are poles apart.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Also used for ideas that are 'a long way apart'.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。也可形容想法或差距很大。

text: 武大郎开店——不容大个儿
pinyin: wǔ dà láng kāi diàn —— bù róng dà gè ér
literal: Wu Dalang · open · shop — not · tolerate · tall · people
natural: Wu Dalang opens a shop and hires no tall people

meaning.en: Short Wu Dalang hires nobody taller than himself; a boss who won't tolerate anyone abler than himself.
meaning.zh: 武大郎身材矮，不用高个子；比喻领导嫉贤妒能，不用比自己强的人。

equivalents: a boss who feels threatened by talent
hire no one better than oneself

examples.zh: 他当主任后把能人都挤走了，真是武大郎开店。
examples.en: Since he became director he's pushed out all the capable ones.

examples.zh: 武大郎开店的单位留不住人才。
examples.en: A firm that shuns talent can't keep good people.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Wu Dalang is the short husband of Pan Jinlian in 《水浒传》; 大个儿 means tall people.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。武大郎是《水浒传》中身材矮小的人物；“大个儿”指高个子。

text: 刘姥姥进大观园——眼花缭乱
pinyin: liú lǎo lao jìn dà guān yuán —— yǎn huā liáo luàn
variants: 刘姥姥进大观园——大开眼界
literal: Granny Liu · enter · Grand View Garden — eyes · dazzled · confused · chaotic
natural: Granny Liu enters the Grand View Garden

meaning.en: The country woman Granny Liu is dazzled by a lavish garden; a person overwhelmed by unfamiliar luxury or novelty.
meaning.zh: 乡下的刘姥姥进了豪华的大观园；比喻没见过世面的人面对新奇事物目不暇接。

equivalents: a country bumpkin in the big city
like a kid in a sweet shop

examples.zh: 第一次逛国际展会，我像刘姥姥进大观园。
examples.en: At my first international expo, I was dazzled by it all.

examples.zh: 他们进了商场，一个个刘姥姥进大观园似的。
examples.en: They walked into the mall wide-eyed.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From 《红楼梦》 (Dream of the Red Chamber).
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自《红楼梦》。

text: 诸葛亮挥泪斩马谡——顾全大局
pinyin: zhū gě liàng huī lèi zhǎn mǎ sù —— gù quán dà jú
literal: Zhuge Liang · wipe · tears · behead · Ma Su — take care of · whole · overall · situation
natural: Zhuge Liang executes Ma Su in tears

meaning.en: Zhuge Liang tearfully executes his favourite Ma Su for losing Jieting; putting the common good before personal feelings.
meaning.zh: 诸葛亮因马谡失街亭而含泪处斩他；比喻为了大局，不徇私情。

equivalents: do the hard thing for the greater good

examples.zh: 为了公司，他诸葛亮挥泪斩马谡，辞退了老友。
examples.en: For the company's sake, he tearfully dismissed his old friend.

examples.zh: 执法要有诸葛亮挥泪斩马谡的魄力。
examples.en: Law enforcement needs the resolve to put justice before friendship.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. From the Three Kingdoms story of the Battle of Jieting.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。出自三国时街亭之战的故事。

pinyin: ā dǒu —— fú bù qǐ lái
literal: Adou — support · not · up
natural: Adou, who cannot be propped up

meaning.en: Liu Chan (nicknamed Adou), the weak last emperor of Shu; someone so incompetent that no help can make them succeed.
meaning.zh: 蜀汉后主刘禅小名阿斗，昏庸无能；比喻无能的人，怎么扶持也没用。

examples.zh: 这孩子就是阿斗，怎么教也不行。
examples.en: That kid is a hopeless case; no teaching works.

examples.zh: 别再帮他了，阿斗是扶不起来的。
examples.en: Stop helping him; he's beyond help.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Often shortened to 扶不起的阿斗.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。常说成“扶不起的阿斗”。

pinyin: làn ní —— fú bù shàng qiáng
literal: rotten mud — support · not · onto · wall
natural: wet mud can't be plastered onto a wall

meaning.en: Soggy mud cannot be made to stick to a wall; a person too hopeless to be helped.
meaning.zh: 烂泥糊不上墙；比喻人不争气，无法扶持。

equivalents: you can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear

examples.zh: 你再给他机会也没用，烂泥扶不上墙。
examples.en: Another chance is pointless; he's a lost cause.

examples.zh: 我劝过多次，他就是烂泥，扶不上墙。
examples.en: I've urged him many times; he's hopeless.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Closely related to Confucius' remark about rotten wood that cannot be carved.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。与孔子“朽木不可雕”之叹意思相近。

pinyin: lǎo shǔ zuān fēng xiāng —— liǎng tóu shòu qì
literal: mouse · bore into · bellows — two · ends · suffer · anger
natural: a mouse stuck in a bellows

meaning.en: A mouse in a bellows is blown at from both ends; stuck between two parties and blamed by both.
meaning.zh: 老鼠钻进风箱，两头都有气；比喻夹在中间，两边受气。

examples.zh: 当中间人，老鼠钻风箱，两头受气。
examples.en: As a go-between I get stick from both sides.

examples.zh: 我夹在老板和客户之间，像老鼠钻风箱。
examples.en: I'm stuck between the boss and the client.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. 气 also means 'bad temper'; the pun is on air from the bellows.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。“气”既指风，也指怨气，形成双关。

pinyin: zhǐ lǎo hǔ —— yī chuō jiù pò
literal: paper · tiger — one · poke · then · break
natural: a paper tiger: one poke and it tears

meaning.en: A tiger made of paper tears at one poke; something that looks fearsome but is actually weak.
meaning.zh: 纸做的老虎，一戳就破；比喻外表强大，实际虚弱。

examples.zh: 别怕他，他不过是纸老虎。
examples.en: Don't be afraid of him; he's just a paper tiger.

examples.zh: 这家公司看着大，其实是纸老虎，一戳就破。
examples.en: The firm looks big but is a paper tiger.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The phrase 纸老虎 alone is the usual form; popularised by Mao Zedong's 'imperialism is a paper tiger'.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。通常只说“纸老虎”，毛泽东“帝国主义是纸老虎”一语使其广为流传。

pinyin: gǎn yā zi shàng jià —— bù dé bù gàn
literal: drive · duck · onto · perch — not · obtain · not · do
natural: driving a duck onto a perch

meaning.en: Forcing a duck up onto a roost, which it cannot manage; being pushed into a task one isn't fit for.
meaning.zh: 把鸭子赶上架，它不会也得上；比喻强迫人做力所不及的事。

equivalents: be thrown in at the deep end

examples.zh: 我不懂管理，完全是被赶鸭子上架。
examples.en: I don't know management; I was just pushed into it.

examples.zh: 别赶鸭子上架，让他先练练。
examples.en: Don't throw him in at the deep end; let him practise first.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Used for being forced into a role; the second half stresses 'having no choice'.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。多指被迫担当某任务；后半句强调别无选择。

text: 老太太吃柿子——专挑软的捏
pinyin: lǎo tài tài chī shì zi —— zhuān tiāo ruǎn de niē
literal: old · lady · eat · persimmon — specially · pick · soft · ones · pinch
natural: an old lady eating persimmons picks the soft ones

meaning.en: An old lady picks the softest persimmon; bullying the weak and avoiding the strong.
meaning.zh: 老太太吃柿子，专拣软的捏；比喻欺负软弱的人。

examples.zh: 你别老太太吃柿子，专挑软的捏。
examples.en: Stop bullying those who can't fight back.

examples.zh: 他对上司唯唯诺诺，对下属老太太吃柿子，专挑软的捏。
examples.en: He's meek with his boss and bullies his subordinates.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The second half is often used alone: 专挑软的捏.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。后半句常单独使用：“专挑软的捏”。

text: 拿着鸡毛当令箭——小题大做
pinyin: ná zhe jī máo dàng lìng jiàn —— xiǎo tí dà zuò
literal: take · chicken · feather · treat as · command · arrow — small · topic · big · do
natural: taking a chicken feather for a command arrow

meaning.en: Treating a chicken feather as a general's command arrow; blowing up a trivial matter or abusing a trifling authority.
meaning.zh: 把鸡毛当作军令；比喻把小事看得很重，或拿着一点小权力当大事。

equivalents: make a mountain out of a molehill

examples.zh: 领导一句话，他就拿着鸡毛当令箭，到处指挥。
examples.en: One remark from the boss and he's giving orders left and right.

examples.zh: 你别拿着鸡毛当令箭，这事没那么严重。
examples.en: Don't blow it out of proportion.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Often used of people who flaunt borrowed authority.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。常指拿着一点权力或上级一句话就摆架子的人。
